Call summary:
- Use case: FinPay wants to add real-time receipt parsing and conversational assistant for payments support (high concurrency, strict latency expectations during business hours).
- Main decision point: appropriate deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem).
- Primary concerns raised: noisy-neighbor effects on shared hosting, isolation boundaries for predictable throughput, and SLO targets (p95/p99 latency, availability).

- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, multi-tenant, strong batching and KV caching to reduce cost. Good for dev/prod start but can see variability under extreme spikes.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with guaranteed throughput, isolation from other tenants, configurable autoscaling and stronger latency SLOs.
- Private VPC/on-prem: full network isolation and customer-controlled infra for regulated data or strict audit requirements.

Attachments: deployment-mode-comparison.xlsx (high-level tradeoffs)

Hi all — quick technical notes to address the FinPay questions. Happy to expand on any point during the deep-dive.

1) Hosted API latency & throughput (typical):
- p50 token latency: ~30–60ms (small generations)
- p95 token latency: ~120–200ms (depends on model and sequence length)
- p99 token latency: ~350–700ms under high concurrency
- Throughput: for typical customer RPCs we see aggregate sustained throughput in the tens of thousands tokens/sec across the service; per-request throughput depends on model size and tokens requested.
Notes: Hosted is multi-tenant but we mitigate variability with continuous batching, prioritized scheduling for premium tiers, and KV/prefix caching which reduces repeated compute. In rare noisy spikes you may see elevated p99s — we offer burst protection and prewarming for predictable schedules.

2) Dedicated capacity isolation:
- Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools (isolated tenancy) — workloads do not share GPUs with other customers.
- Scheduling: we allocate whole-node/partition assignments and use container-level resource controls (cgroups) plus runtime throttling to avoid cross-tenant interference.
- SLOs: Dedicated customers can opt into 99.9% availability and latency-backed SLOs at the route level (we'll attach the SLA PDF).
- No noisy neighbor: since GPUs are reserved to your pool, noisy-neighbor effects are effectively eliminated at the GPU level. Any residual variability is on networking or host-level transient events which we detect and remediate automatically.

3) Network & data isolation / compliance: 
- VPC peering & private endpoints available for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- KMS integration for customer-managed keys supported in Dedicated and Private flows.
- Logging & audit: request logs and KV caches are logically separated per-tenant; for Dedicated we provide dedicated storage partitions and optional longer audit retention.

4) Practical guidance & next steps:
- If FinPay's production traffic is user-facing with tight SLOs and predictable business-hour peaks, Dedicated is the recommended path for initial rollout.
- We can run a short Dedicated pilot (72–168 hours) with traffic replay to validate p95/p99 under your workload.
- For the deep-dive I can bring sample telemetry (p95/p99 curves) and walk through rollout/canary plans.

Attaching: redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf

Happy to join Wed 2/23 10–12 PT — confirming availability.
